title: Filtered derived Hom, truncations and the graded obstruction complex
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with enough injectives (every object embeds into an object $I$ for which $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(-,I)$ is exact), with localizations and Hom groups taken in a common larger universe. Write $DF^b(\mathcal A)$ for the localization of bounded cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] equipped with finite decreasing filtrations by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration, def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients], at maps which are quasi-isomorphisms on every graded complex. Write $\omega$ for forgetting the filtration and $\operatorname{gr}^aP=F^aP/F^{a+1}P$. Filtration bounds refer to filtration indices, independently of cochain degrees. The same notation with $+$ permits bounded-below complexes, still with finite filtrations.

For every integer $r$, the filtration truncations $t_{\ge r}P=F^rP$ and $t_{<r}P=P/F^rP$, with their induced filtrations, descend to exact functors on these localizations and give natural distinguished triangles
$$t_{\ge r}P\longrightarrow P\longrightarrow t_{<r}P\longrightarrow(t_{\ge r}P)[1].$$
The first map is the inclusion and the second is the quotient before localization. The triangle is uniquely determined, up to unique isomorphism inducing the identity on $P$, among distinguished triangles $L\to P\to R\to L[1]$ for which $\operatorname{gr}^aL=0$ for $a<r$ and $\operatorname{gr}^aR=0$ for $a\ge r$. These triangles are functorial for every morphism in the filtered derived category; after applying $\omega$ they induce the corresponding underlying triangles and their subobject and quotient maps.

There is a filtered derived global Hom bifunctor $H=R\operatorname{Hom}_F(P,Q)$, for $P,Q\in DF^b(\mathcal A)$, with values in $DF^+(\mathbf{Ab})$, such that naturally
$$\omega H\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(\omega P,\omega Q),\qquad
\operatorname{gr}^rH\simeq\bigoplus_a R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(\operatorname{gr}^aP,\operatorname{gr}^{a+r}Q).$$
Here ordinary global derived Hom is the derived Hom complex of abelian groups, whose $q$-th cohomology is $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(\omega P,\omega Q[q])$ (and likewise for its graded arguments). The sum is finite. Moreover
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{DF(\mathcal A)}(P,Q)\simeq H^0(\omega t_{\ge0}H).$$
The forgetful map to $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(\omega P,\omega Q)$ is $H^0$ of the inclusion $\omega t_{\ge0}H\to\omega H$. Under the displayed graded comparison, the components of the projection of a filtered morphism to $H^0(\operatorname{gr}^0H)$ are its morphisms $\operatorname{gr}^aP\to\operatorname{gr}^aQ$.

proof.text: Take the existing calculus with canonical coefficient universe max(u,v). For the enlarged coefficient category Ab at max(s,u,v), obtain its cone-normalized bounded-below localization and representative-normalized truncation calculus from the same existing calculus applied to abelian groups. The original bounded and plus structures on A are retained.

Apply exact finite-filtered coefficient change to the exact additive universe-lift functor Ab(max(u,v))→Ab(max(s,u,v)). This gives the filtered coefficient functor, its forgetful and graded comparisons, and the high-zero comparison preserving the actual inclusion and grade-zero quotient projection.

Postcompose ordinary Hom with the ordinary derived coefficient functor and filtered Hom with the filtered coefficient functor. Exact universe lift commutes with homology, by the natural homology isomorphism on complexes descended through localization. Compose that isomorphism with ULift.down and the existing additive Hom bijection. Naturality follows from the natural isomorphism. The canonical double-ULift isomorphism identifies the ordinary Hom-complex model with the single lift required by the unchanged signature.

Transport the graded finite-support bilimit bicone through the additive derived coefficient functor: restrict to the finite support, use preservation of finite biproducts, then extend the limit and colimit over the remaining zero summands. This also treats empty support. Compose the graded comparison from coefficient change with the old graded comparison.

Define the filtered-morphism additive equivalence by the high-zero homology comparison and the old equivalence. Naturality follows from the comparison. Evaluate the two coefficient-change squares on H⁰, using the natural ordinary homology comparison. The old forgetful-map and graded-projection equations then give exactly the new equations, with the same shifts and associated graded maps.

The 5.1.1(c) adjoint-direction source error is confirmed by k in grade 0 vs grade 1, and the item never uses that sentence. Checked every step by hand. Step 1: the filtered cylinder squares to zero and its graded kernel is a contractible identity cone. Step 3, repaired: the cone-to-quotient contraction (y,x)->(0,y) works; the vanishing Hom(L,R[q])=0 follows from the unbounded-truncation bijection with M=R[q]; full faithfulness transfers it to the bounded categories; triangle-morphism-extension (1)(c) and (2) with q=0 and q=-1 give uniqueness, and reversing the triangles gives the isomorphism. Step 4: filtration bounds c-b and e-a+1, lower bound w-v and the cocycle/boundary signs are right. Step 5: the kernel is F^{r+1}, and surjectivity by injective extension holds in all three grade cases. Step 6, repaired: it uses exactly the new node's clauses, with one-variable descent by the localization universal property (1)-(3). Step 7: the H^0, forgetful-map and gr^0 identifications hold. New node: the homotopy formulas S(f)=(-1)^n f h and T(f)=k f check out, and the graded quasi-isomorphism clause holds by the termwise split flags, the graded Hom decomposition and 070J K-injectivity, with finite sums because P is bounded. It is statement-only and self-contained, not a clause of the item, and not a duplicate (the closest is lem-trf-hom-dual-preserves-homotopies, which is unfiltered and covers only homotopies). Accepted all five declared tool uses as generic homological algebra: injective-model, triangle-morphism-extension, injective-graded-filtration-splits, filtered-unbounded-truncation, filtered-bounded-localization-comparison.
